newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-LAKERS WIN AGAIN WITHOUT SHAQ.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-LAKERS WIN AGAIN WITHOUT SHAQ.

text.p: Even without Shaq, the show must go on, and the Los Angeles Lakers rolled to their second straight win without their star Thursday, crushing the Denver Nuggets 132-117.

Nick Van Exel scored 30 points and matched a team record with eight three-pointers as the Lakers cruised to their ninth win in 10 games, but the win was dampened by the news earlier in the day that Shaquille O'Neal will be out at least eight weeks with ligament damage in his left knee.

Eddie Jones scored 22 points and Elden Campbell, playing centre in O'Neal's place for a second strong game in a row, added 19 for the Lakers, who are three games ahead of the Seattle SuperSonics for the lead in the Pacific Division.
"When we play without Shaq it's like a Broadway play and Elden is the understudy and the play goes on," Los Angeles coach Del Harris said.

"I played centre before and it felt good being the go-to guy," Campbell said. "We played some good defence tonight to set the tone. We broke their spirit and did a good job until the very end when it didn't matter anymore."
Van Exel, who shot 8-for-13 from three-point range, also made eight three-pointers at Dallas in 1994.

"I was feeling it tonight," Van Exel said. "Without Shaq I have to be a little more creative and get the guys active. It seems like they didn't play hard, like they just gave up. I think we can still get the top spot in the Western Conference" without O'Neal.
The Lakers' 132 points matched the NBA season high set by the Nuggets against the New Jersey Nets on January 20.
"We just moved the ball well," Harris said. "We're one of the better scoring teams in the league."
Bryant Stith scored 26 points and Antonio McDyess added 23 points and nine rebounds for the Nuggets, who have lost three of their last five games.
In Miami, Alonzo Mourning scored 29 points and grabbed 13 rebounds to lead the Heat to their eighth straight victory, 106-90 over the Indiana Pacers.

The Pacers led 24-23 at the end of the first quarter, but Miami took control with a 21-2 run in the second that featured a string of four three-pointers. Voshon Lenard hit the first and last and Keith Atkins and Tim Hardaway nailed the others. The Heat went into halftime with a 57-34 lead.
"We simply had one of the best quarters this season," Heat coach Pat Riley said. "That was the best we've run our offence."
"It got contagious," Hardaway said. "We started rolling.

Hardaway finished with 18 points, 14 assists and four steals and Askins hit for a season-high 15 points for Miami, which avenged a 103-89 home loss to Indiana. Lenard rebounded from a scoreless effort against Detroit Tuesday with 20 points.
In Dallas, Latrell Sprewell had 28 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Golden State Warriors pulled away late for a 107-99 victory over the Mavericks, snapping a four-game losing streak.
Joe Smith added 20 points and 12 rebounds for the Warriors.
Chris Gatling, making his first start of the season, had 19 points and 13 rebounds and Sam Cassell added 18 points, seven rebounds and five steals for Dallas.
At Utah, Jeff Hornacek scored 10 of his 16 points during a pivotal 25-0 third-quarter burst as the Jazz won their fourth straight game, routing the Portland Trail Blazers 110-86.

Hornacek had 10 points and Bryon Russell added five as the Jazz turned a 53-47 edge into a 31-point lead with 4:32 to play in the quarter. Karl Malone led Utah with 24 points and 11 rebounds and John Stockton added 17 and 13 assists.
In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond scored a season-high 41 points and Olden Polynice added 17 points and 13 rebounds as the Kings beat the Los Angeles Clippers 105-98.
Richmond tied his season high with seven three-pointers and led the team in scoring for the 11th straight game. The Kings snapped a three-game losing streak.
Malik Sealy scored 20 points and Loy Vaught chipped in 17 and eight rebounds for the Clippers, who had their winning streak snapped at a season-high five games.
In New York, Allan Houston scored 28 points and Charles Oakley added 21 -- all in the second half -- as the Knicks defeated the Philadelphia 76ers 107-92.
Patrick Ewing added 17 points as New York defeated Philadelphia for the 26th time in its last 33 meetings.

Jerry Stackhouse led Philadelphia with 20 points but rookie point guard Allen Iverson, who torched the Knicks for 83 points in the first three meetings this season, was held to 13 on 4-for-19 shooting.
